From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: LinqPay Ops <ops@linqpay.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: LLM fit readout — acceptance runbook and next-run

Hi Sam — great meeting today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a proposed runbook so we can scope a short evaluation sprint (3 weeks) to validate parity vs LexiCore-v3 and a recommended open candidate.

Summary of findings from demo:
- Primary intents (payments, dispute triage, account lookup) mapped to high-quality examples; LexiCore-v3 currently reports ~93% intent accuracy on your QA set (per Sam).
- Two failure modes flagged: hallucination on bank-name extraction (~1.8% in baseline) and verbosity/incorrect regulatory citations in dispute explanations.

Redwood candidate models to trial (recommend ordered):
1) open-llama3-70b-instruct (quantized 4-bit) — strong coverage on instruction-following, expect p50 latency ~220ms on our Dedicated pool with 8k context
2) redwood-q8k-30b (our optimized open variant) — lower cost, good for slot-filling and structured outputs
3) hybrid fallback -> LexiCore-lite (proprietary baseline) for high-risk regulatory responses during canary

Acceptance gates (proposed):
- Intent accuracy >= 95% (blind eval vs labeled sample of 2k utterances)
- Hallucination (incorrect facts or bank-entity invented) < 2% on the same sample
- Response latency p50 < 250ms, p95 < 800ms in Dedicated environment
- No regressions on the four safety prompt templates you supplied (regulatory citation tests)

Planned sprint (attached: llm-sprint-specs.xlsx):
- Week 0: Prep prompt bundle + dataset (we'll use prompt-bundle-v1.jsonl and your anonymized logs subset)
- Week 1: A/B blind run vs LexiCore-v3 (randomized assignment) — collect metrics and human ratings
- Week 2: Model tuning (prompt engineering + light instruction-tuning if needed) + canary deployment to 5% traffic
- Decision: If all gates pass -> expand to 50% + schedule rollout; if not -> fallback + root-cause doc

Benchmarks: see attached 'benchmarks-abridged.pdf' for proxy metrics we expect and the Drive folder link in related links for raw dashboards.

Next asks from LinqPay to proceed:
1) Confirm dataset access window and sampling (we asked for 2k labeled utterances + 20k anonymized logs)
2) Sign the evaluation SOW (DocuSign link below)
3) A short Ops contact for canary coordination (time windows, throttles)

I'll wait for a quick thumbs-up on the dataset and canary windows and we can lock dates.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0142

Thanks Tessa — this looks actionable and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications before we lock sprint dates:

- LexiCore-v3 baseline: the 93% intent accuracy I quoted is on our internal test harness (not the final production mix); we'll produce the labeled 2k this week.
- Latency expectation: our production SLA aims for p50 < 200ms for snappy flows; curious if you expect open-llama3-70b to hit that at peak (we can stagger traffic).
- Regulatory responses: can you scope a strict fallback rule that routes any response with 'legal' or 'dispute' taxonomy to LexiCore-lite until we validate citations? That would keep high-risk traffic guarded.

Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: evaluation plan notes and riff on gates

Tessa / Neha — internal follow-up after Sam's reply. Key technical adjustments I'd propose before we ask for dataset: 

1) Latency: open-llama3-70b will likely be ~210-240ms p50 on Dedicated with our current kernel selection for 8k context. To reach p50 < 200ms we'd need either more dedicated shard capacity or to test redwood-q8k-30b tuned to smaller context windows (4k). Recommend we offer two canary profiles: low-latency (q8k-30b) and high-quality (llama3-70b) and split traffic accordingly.

2) Blind A/B design: 2k labeled utterances -> split 60/40 (candidate / baseline) for powered stats; human raters use 3-pt scale (Correct / Partial / Incorrect) plus a binary hallucination flag. We'll target 95% power to detect 2.5% diff in intent accuracy.

3) Safety fallback rule: implement tag-based routing in our Smart Router: any message with taxonomy {"regulatory","dispute","refund_claim"} => route to LexiCore-lite by default for first canary week. If candidate passes citation gate, relax rule for subsequent canary.

4) Data retention & privacy: request confirmation that LinqPay will accept our standard test-data DPA for ephemeral storage of logs (7 days) used only for eval.

I'll prepare the A/B assignment script and a quick Jupyter notebook to produce the initial acceptance report. Dropping the Drive link to the evaluation playbook (see related_links).

-Ben

Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
